Canny

/KAN-ee/ - rhymes with granny · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Canny means shrewd and careful in practical matters.

The canny landlady rents the ground floor to a bakery at a discount — the smell of warm bread has sold every unit upstairs.

Worked Example

Rosa's food truck skips the county fair every year. The pitch fees there eat a week's profit, so instead she parks at the marathon finish line, where four thousand hungry runners funnel past exactly one vendor. She studies foot-traffic maps in January the way other cooks study recipes. Nothing about the plan is flashy; all of it works.

Canny is the exact word for Rosa because it means shrewd and careful in practical matters — judgment applied where money, timing, and people actually move. A brilliant cook might still choose the wrong corner. The canny one reads the situation first, risks little, and quietly comes out ahead.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

shrewd: Shrewd praises sharp judgment — a shrewd reader of people and situations sees the angle others miss. Canny takes that sharpness and adds a careful, self-protecting streak: it hedges, risks little, and quietly banks the advantage. A shrewd move can be bold; a canny one rarely is.

savvy: Savvy is insider fluency — the practical know-how you earn from years inside one particular scene or trade, the way a roadie or a day trader knows their world. Canny needs no résumé: it is careful, sharp-eyed practical judgment that travels, working in situations its owner has never met before.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

gullible: swallows whatever it is told

naive: trusts easily out of inexperience

Where it sits · how far sharp dealing shades into trickery — sensible → canny → crafty

sensible vs. canny: A sensible buyer avoids the obvious mistakes; a canny one goes further, reading angles and timing that most people never notice.

crafty vs. canny: Crafty goes past canny into tricks and misdirection — the canny operator plays the odds sharply but plays them fair.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cann

Root — cann: to know how (Scots and northern English can, ken)

Suffix — -y

Suffix — -y: full of, marked by

Put it together

Put it together: Cann- (to know how) + -y (marked by) = marked by know-how. The word walked south out of Scotland, where can and ken both meant knowing — a canny dealer was one who kent the trade. English kept the sense: practical knowing, applied carefully.

Use the root in a new word: ken

Use the root in a new word: ken: The lawsuit's tax arithmetic was beyond my ken, so I stopped nodding and hired an accountant.

Word Choice

neutral / slightly informal

Reach for canny when someone reads the practical angles — prices, timing, what the other side will do next — and plays them carefully to their own advantage. This unit's judicious weighs every interest and picks the soundest course; canny keeps one eye on its own side of the ledger. And if real trickery enters, you've left canny for crafty.
